subject: Gating and semver for runtime-config + feature-flag APIs
messages:
From: Evan Park <evan@opsly.io>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Request: gating window & semver for runtime-config / feature-flags

Hi Camila,

Hope you’re well — Evan from Opsly. We’ve been using the Redwood SDK in production for our runtime feature flags and dynamic configuration (endpoints: /v1/runtime-config and /v1/feature-flags). We shipped last quarter and are seeing steady traffic (attached opsly-prod-usage.csv for the last 30 days).

Opsly is planning a platform release in Q1 and needs stronger guarantees around API stability and deprecation timelines. We saw notes about an upcoming cleanup/deprecation pass in the Redwood roadmap and wanted to put a formal request on the table:

- A clear semver policy for public runtime/config endpoints (what constitutes a major vs minor change)
- A 6-month grace period for breaking changes to those endpoints (or an equivalent canary/compatibility mechanism)
- A defined SDK bump schedule and migration guide so we can plan engineering cycles

We’d love to understand Redwood’s proposed approach (gating, canary endpoints, headers for compatibility, etc.) and the contact on the Redwood side who can own the technical contract.

Attaching: opsly-prod-usage.csv

Thanks,
Evan Park
Platform Integrations
Opsly
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Park <evan@opsly.io>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: gating window & semver for runtime-config / feature-flags

Hi Evan — thanks for the clear ask and for the usage export. I’ve looped in Jonas (solutions eng) and Vanessa (partner ops) to evaluate technical and program implications.

Next steps from our side:
- Jonas will draft a compatibility and versioning proposal with concrete timelines and migration controls.
- We’ll propose a mutually agreeable gating cadence (canary + gradual rollout) and document an SDK migration path.
- I’ll set up a 30-min sync early next week to walk through options.

Can you share any internal deadlines for your Q1 release (week range) so we can align?

Best,
Camila Reyes
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Evan Park <evan@opsly.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: gating window & semver for runtime-config / feature-flags

Evan, Camila — I reviewed the endpoints and your usage pattern. Short summary and options below. Attaching a concise proposed-versioning-plan.pdf with timelines and example headers.

Context / risk
- The runtime-config and feature-flag endpoints are used in-line in many of your requests and often gate user-facing behavior; a breaking change can cause widespread failure if apps auto-upgrade.
- We currently have internal cleanup planned that touches response shape and a small set of query parameters. Those changes could be major if we remove fields.

Options we recommend (trade-offs):
1) Soft deprecation + compatibility header (lower engineering cost)
   - Add header X-Redwood-Compat: v1.0 to opt-in to v1 semantics by default.
   - Non-breaking changes: documented as minor (90-day notice).
   - Breaking changes: require major bump + 180-day deprecation with automatic compatibility middleware for 60 days.

2) SemVer+Canary (higher operational overhead, best for partners at scale)
   - Publish /v1/ and /v2/ simultaneously. Traffic split via canary route and feature flag.
   - SDKs released with pinned semver and opt-in runtime for new behavior.
   - Major change enforced only on /v2; /v1 preserved for at least 180 days after v2 GA.

Proposed pragmatic plan for Opsly (to balance our roadmap and your ask):
- Publish a formal migration plan by Oct 17 (migration guide + SDK bump notes).
- Provide a canary endpoint (canary.redwood.ai/runtime-config) by Nov 1 for early testing.
- Adopt semver for public runtime APIs; mark breaking changes as major with a 180-day public deprecation period.
- For minor/non-breaking updates, we will give 90 days notice and a backward compatibility header option.

Attachments: proposed-versioning-plan.pdf

If that looks acceptable, we’ll lock dates and start the SOW language for support/paid migration assistance if you want dedicated help.

— Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Evan Park <evan@opsly.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: gating window & semver for runtime-config / feature-flags

Thanks Jonas — this is helpful. Opsly’s position: we are comfortable with the semver + canary approach but need the following commitments prior to locking our Q1 launch date:

- A 6-month (180 day) guaranteed support window for /v1 after /v2 GA, with a clearly published deprecation date.
- A short-term compatibility shim or header for SDKs (we request at least 90 days of automatic compatibility behavior for the most-used fields).
- Migration guide + SDK examples (server and browser) delivered by Oct 17 as you suggested.
- Canary endpoint accessible to us from Nov 1; we’d like a 2-week canary window where we can opt-in a percentage of traffic alongside Redwood engineers.

One ask on the commercial side: can the 180-day guarantee be added into our integration SOW / addendum (we can push this via legal as a narrow operational SLA)? Happy to share an Opsly draft.

If we get these points agreed, Opsly will commit to the integration support package (this is a gating dependency for our Q1 roadmap).

Regards,
Evan
Platform Integrations, Opsly
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Park <evan@opsly.io>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 03 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: gating window & semver for runtime-config / feature-flags

Evan — thanks, and appreciate the clarity. Confirming Redwood’s mutual action plan below so we can update the HubSpot deal and craft the SOW language:

Mutual action plan (agreed)
- Redwood will publish the migration guide and SDK examples by 2026-10-17 (docs + code samples).
- Redwood will spin up the canary endpoint on 2026-11-01 and open a 14-day canary testing window where Opsly and Redwood can split traffic and validate.
- Semantic versioning policy: major bump required for breaking changes; Redwood will maintain /v1 for at least 180 days after /v2 GA and publish the deprecation date at GA.
- Compatibility header/short-term shim: Redwood will provide an opt-in header and a 90-day automatic compatibility shim for removed fields; details to be in the migration guide.
- Commercial: I’ll ask Legal to draft narrow SOW language that captures the 180-day operational guarantee for the runtime endpoints; please send Opsly’s redline if you have one.

Next steps
- Jonas: finalize the proposed-versioning-plan.pdf and post it to the shared Drive link.
- Vanessa: update HubSpot (deal OPSLY-2026-374) with the mutual action plan and attach attachments + timeline.
- Opsly: send any legal redlines and confirm availability for a quick call on 2026-10-06 at 11:00 PT to finalize the canary run plan.

Links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890 | https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2B3C4D5E6F
